points.claim: This round's metrics do not measure round 16 as it was played. The files in metrics/ were regenerated by replaying round 16's typed lines against the world as revised after round 16, at Sprout 2c85fd7. In at least two replays the world's answers changed and the run drifted away from the recording, so later lines land in the wrong rooms. In newcomer, 'open the window wider' got not_here in play and is no longer refused in the replay. The window is then already open, the player climbs back out, and from turn 13 on almost every line is not_here: 'take the sack and the bottle' at turn 13 answered 'Brown sack: Taken.' in play. In goal-seeker, the replay follows the recording to about turn 108, where 'go up' in the Cellar now prints the round-16 bar rule. After that it drifts: 'take bar' is not_here at turn 112, and from turn 119 it gets dozens of 'The forest becomes impenetrable' and not_here lines where the recording was underground. So the round's jumps (unreadRate 0.07 to 0.45, repetition 20 to 65, places never reached 41 to 58, passages never reached 1692 to 1742) come mostly from the replay drifting. The world did not get worse. As played and first recorded in this round's synthesis.md, round 16 was unreadRate 0.14, refusedRate 0.02, repetition 43, places never reached 27, objects never reached 550, verbs never reached 68, handlers never reached 79, passages never reached 1707. The echo lines also changed case, 'North north ...' in play to 'north north ...' in the replay, which the author should check is intended.

evidence.quote: recorded: 'open the window wider' -> You can't see any such thing. Replay: not refused; at the next 'open the window' the replay says 'It is already open.'
replay: 'take the sack and the bottle' -> You can't see any such thing. (recorded: 'Brown sack: Taken. / Glass bottle: Taken.')
replay: 'take the lantern and the sword' -> You can't see any such thing.
replay: 'go up' -> The trap door is closed. Whoever keeps the bar up there drops it behind anyone new to the house... (the round-16 revision's line, not seen in play)
replay: 'take bar' -> You can't see any such thing.
replay: 'go north' -> The forest becomes impenetrable to the north. (many such lines follow)
recorded 'North north ...' (kind refused); replay 'north north ...' counted unread

points.recommendation: Don't judge the round-16 revision by these deltas. Compute a round's metrics at the revision and Sprout pin the round was played at (revision.json, sprout.pin.json at that time). If replays must run against a newer world, have the replay stop or flag at the first step whose output differs from the recorded `expect`, and count only the steps before it. File this with the studio's metrics tooling. Don't file it against the world.

points.claim: Round 15's trap-door line was never read. It shows only when the door is examined from the Cellar, and nobody examined it. Four runs tried the barred door from below with up, open, push open and smash, and got Zork's bare refusals. They went on ferrying treasure up the chimney one item at a time: newcomer made five climbs, and parser-breaker quit bored and gave this as the reason. (The revision already moved the rule onto these refusals. The figures in P1 show the replay reading it at goal-seeker turn 108.)

evidence.quote: go up -> The trap door is closed.
push open the trap door -> The door is locked from above.
open trap door -> The door is locked from above.
smash the trap door with the platinum bar -> Nice try.
report: 'the walk up the chimney with one item per trip was getting repetitive'

points.recommendation: Keep TOUCHBIT. The rule now follows each refusal where players meet the bar. Round 17 should check whether a player who reads it goes looking for another road home.

points.claim: The trap door's open state had no voice. goal-seeker came up by prayer, opened the trap door from above, and went down; it stayed open, as intended. Later, carrying the skull, it walked through the Cellar under the open door to the chimney, which refused its load. The Cellar's BRIEF line never said the door was open. Its report still wishes it could 'unbar the trap door from below'.

evidence.quote: pray -> Forest
go down -> Cellar (no crash)
go up (Studio) -> You can't get up there with what you're carrying...
after the slide, go up -> Living Room

points.recommendation: Accepted in the revision: the Cellar now says 'The trap door above you stands open.' Round 17 should watch whether a returning player takes the stairs instead of the chimney.

points.claim: The torch went unused at the shaft for the third round running. No run reached the lower mine. goal-seeker put the torch back in the case just before heading for the mine, went through the Gas Room with only the lamp, and spent its last turns in the coal mine maze. No run examined the shaft.

evidence.quote: put torch in case -> Done.
report: 'The coal mine is a maze of identical nondescript rooms.'
examined the basket; the shaft never examined

points.recommendation: No world change; the shaft and torch already point at each other. Testing the diamond needs a run aimed at the mine or one that starts mid-game. That is the director's call.

points.claim: The mazes used up the long runs' turns. prose-reader spent turns 151 to 240 in Zork's Maze. It reached the Grating Room holding the key, stepped straight back out, and never found it again. goal-seeker ended lost in the coal mine. Neither marked rooms by dropping things. Their no_way lines are most of the unread and repetition counts as played.

evidence.quote: go northeast -> Grating Room ... a grating locked with a skull-and-crossbones lock.
go southwest -> Maze
report: 'Once I found the grating room I overshot it and could never find it again.'
lost in the coal mine

points.recommendation: Keep the maze and mine as Zork built them. Count maze and mine no_way lines separately when reading unreadRate and repetition.

points.claim: The thief robbed three runs and was read correctly, as an unseen someone. He took the jade from the Studio floor in newcomer's run, and took the trident and bracelet from prose-reader before killing it. Nobody went after him, and the Cyclops, the Strange Passage and the Treasure Room were not reached.

The thief, a pragmatist, dispatches you as a threat to his livelihood.
he quietly abstracted some valuables from your possession
Finding nothing of value, he left disgruntled.

empty sack -> That sentence isn't one I recognize.

points.recommendation: Friction 120 and 132; the evidence is logged. Note that the pin at 2c85fd7 seems to accept 'open the window wider' now (P1). If it does, record that against friction 120.

points.claim: Players took Zork's own text for the world's changes: the Round Room's cave-ins and the Dam's west exit. Both are original. The 'changed version' framing sends players looking for alterations.

evidence.quote: report: 'The Round Room says several passages are blocked by cave-ins, so the map isn't what I expected.'
report: 'first sign this isn't quite the place I remembered'
report: 'Some of the map is altered too'

points.recommendation: No world change. This is the director's concern about the framing.

points.claim: What was reached worked and was praised. Five runs quoted the trophy case's 'patient air' as the goal, and four called the chimney's rule clear and fair. The exorcism ran in order and to its clock, the lamp dimmed, the canyon was climbed, the slide and the stairs were used to get home, and the pot of gold appeared. Still unmet: death as a spirit, the bottle refilled, the grating taking small things, the grue, the egg given to the thief, the grating opened from below, and the 350 ending.

evidence.quote: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
"Begone, fiends!" ... the spirits ... flee through the walls.
the rainbow appears to become solid
report: 'told me what the game wants from me without a tutorial'

points.claim: The goal 'Get as high a score as you can': goal-seeker did not reach 350. Its 225, rank Adventurer, at turn 353 is the best score of any round; round 15's best was 164. The 400-turn cap stopped it in the coal mine at turn 398. Its losses were the walk past the open trap door to the chimney (P3), the torch back in the case before the mine (P4), the mine's maze (P5), and the thief's lair, the Cyclops, the river and the diamond left untouched. Two other runs met their own aims: explorer cased the egg whole and stopped at 60, and newcomer cased four treasures for 95.

evidence.quote: Your score is 225 (total of 350 points), in 311 moves. This gives you the rank of Adventurer.
report: 'I ran out of turns while lost in the coal mine maze.'
put egg in trophy case -> Done.
score 95 of 350

points.recommendation: P2 and P3, both made in the revision, are the levers on the score. The 350 ending needs a longer cap or a mid-game start, which is the director's call.

legibility.why: All six read the world as a treasure hunt under the white house, filling a case that 'expects to be filled'. Five also read the deliberate extra presence (the barring 'someone', 'somebody tidy', the unseen thief) and the hauling puzzle, as the intent hopes. explorer read the egg's clasp as the thief's job, which is the intended way to the canary. casual matches only in part: it had 30 turns, and it took Zork's own cave-ins for the alteration.

runs.understood: The white house with a trophy case that wants filling, treasure above and below, and fragile treasures someone dishonest might want; the egg's clasp is for a thief's fingers.
A treasure hunt whose real game is logistics: carrying limits, one-way routes, a one-thing chimney and a trap door barred behind you.
Treasure under a house, where getting it home is half the job; a barred trap door, a narrow chimney, and somebody unseen who takes what you leave lying around.
Classic Zork: treasures for a case, 'altered somewhere underground'. It took the cave-ins and the barred door for the changes and did not get far enough to see more.
The old map in a wry, melancholy voice about the adventurers who came before and didn't make it home.
A world that says no politely, whose changes are about carrying: scattered belongings after death, 'somebody tidy', the chimney's limit.
